note: Set A covers the page broadly and correctly captures the dinner-party safety rules (alcohol, water source, cookware washing, grilling/cooler restrictions), the meal location and hors d'oeuvres permission, and the non-decathlete restriction, all with supporting quotes. Set B is clean but extremely narrow: all 12 claims restate only four facts (TV/computer display sizes, TV brightness, guest count) with heavy duplication, omitting nearly all of Rule 9-3k safety requirements and the meal rules. Set A's flaws are a misbound condition on the flame ban ('during cooking' instead of 'during contest week'), one unsupported 'TV display | brightness | maximum' claim, and a misquoted 'open flames' wording, plus many redundant restatements. Because missing most of the page's substantive requirements counts against B, A is the better set despite its few errors.
